entities.summary: Zvonimir Šeparović was a Croatian jurist and politician who played a crucial role in the transition of Yugoslavia from a socialist state to a federal republic in the 1990s. Born in Blato, Korčula, on September 14, 1928, Šeparović was a key figure in the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), a party that dominated Croatian politics during the 1990s. As a leading jurist, he was instrumental in drafting the Croatian Constitution and the European Convention on Human Rights. Šeparović's legacy extends beyond Croatia, as his work on European integration and human rights has influenced policymakers and scholars across the continent. His dedication to democratic values and the rule of law has left a lasting impact on the region. The irony of his passing in 2022, just as the European Union was strengthening its ties with Croatia, underscores the significance of his contributions to European politics and human rights.
